paragraphs: Close to 500 people joined a protest in Midleton, Co Cork, on Saturday. They want better protection from floods.
In October 2023, Storm Babet brought very heavy rain. Water filled homes and shops in the town. In some places, it was 1.5 metres deep. The damage cost up to 200 million euro.
People say they still feel in danger. A local group says the flood plan keeps getting delayed. They have now heard four different dates.

The Government says it is spending 14 million euro in the area. Some new works will start next spring. The full plan should go to planning by the end of the year. It will protect 750 homes and businesses.
Nearly 500 people took part in a protest in Midleton, Co Cork, on Saturday. They say the town still has no real protection from floods, three years after Storm Babet.
In October 2023, extreme rain hit Midleton and other parts of east Cork. Water up to 1.5 metres deep flooded homes and businesses, causing up to 200 million euro in damage.

Mona Stromsoe, a spokeswoman for the local flood protection group, said people feel as unsafe as they did in 2023. The group was told the main flood plan would go to planning in September, but this did not happen. It has now been given four different dates. She said a summer flood in Killarney showed how quickly it can happen again.

Minister of State Kevin Moran says 14 million euro has been set aside for Midleton and east Cork. Work to protect 135 properties will start next spring. Cork County Council plans to apply for planning permission for the full scheme by the end of the year. The scheme would protect 750 properties.
Close to 500 people marched through Midleton, Co Cork, on Saturday to protest at what they described as a lack of meaningful flood protection since Storm Babet struck the town in 2023.

Extreme rainfall in October 2023 left parts of Midleton under as much as 1.5 metres of water, causing up to 200 million euro worth of damage to homes and businesses. Residents from nearby villages, including Mogeely, Killeagh and Castlemartyr, also joined the protest.

Mona Stromsoe of the Midleton and East Cork Flood Protection Group said locals feel just as vulnerable as they did three years ago. The group had been told in July that the flood relief scheme would be submitted for planning at the end of September, but that deadline was missed, and the date has now been pushed back for the fourth time.

Minister of State Kevin Moran has pointed to a 14 million euro allocation for the area, including 5.8 million euro for advance works that will protect 135 properties from next spring.
